result.title: Interpretable Graph Partitioning for Spatial Prediction
result.summary: Spatial prediction estimates unobserved values from spatially distributed observations. Although flexible predictive models are increasingly available, their practical use remains limited when interpretability is essential. In this study, we formulate a graph partitioning problem to construct a global surrogate model that approximates black-box predictions with simpler representations. Specifically, we select connected subgraphs to minimize within-cluster residuals in vertex-level predictions. Although this formulation can be viewed as a variant of spatial regionalization, it operates on model-based predictions at individual locations rather than predefined areal units. With many locations, this point-level formulation may produce artificial connections between regions, reducing interpretability. We therefore introduce a constraint that excludes such connections while retaining flexible partition boundaries. We theoretically analyze how this constraint affects the resulting partition. We also develop a computational procedure for adjusting partition boundaries. Experimental results show that the proposed method yields spatially coherent partitions with flexible boundaries.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把空间预测的可解释性表述为图划分问题：用连通子图构建逼近黑箱预测的全局代理模型，以簇内残差最小化为目标，并引入排除人工连接的约束，给出该约束对划分影响的理论分析和边界调整算法，实验得到空间连贯且边界灵活的划分。
AI.relevance_reason: 属空间统计中的代理建模与区域化，与 VLM 推理无直接关联；但其按残差最小化把预测空间切成连贯可解释单元的图划分思路，可能对 LVR 中把内部状态或视觉证据切分为可解释、可检验单元（状态抽象、证据筛选）的表述有所启发，可供核查，迁移性尚不确定。
